rules.name: Idle timer is armed only when quiescent
consequences: Every schedule first cancels any existing timer (timer_pending=false)
then arms a fresh timer (timer_pending=true) iff condition holds
schedule points: end of load_model, end of each request, end of reload, idle timer re-arm

rules.name: Active requests suspend auto-unload
consequences: active_requests increments and the idle timer is cancelled
on request end active_requests decrements, last_used is stamped and the timer is rescheduled

rules.name: Timer firing unloads only a quiescent, genuinely idle backend
consequences: backend released, last_used stamped, cache flushed if CUDA, log line with configured timeout
if not idle_expired the timer re-arms instead
timer handle stays set (done task) after a firing that unloads

rules.name: Backend is lazily re-created on demand
rules.condition: !backend_loaded when ensure_backend runs (double-checked under the lock)

rules.name: Unload is idempotent
consequences: no state change (last_used not stamped), no error; CUDA cache still flushed if available

unknowns.what: load_model omitted from ensure_backend's executable steps
unknowns.why: Both tests that reach the lazy-reload path (concurrency test, test_generate_lazy_reinit_when_backend_none) patch load_model with a stand-in, so its real decision sites are not executed there. The real production path would additionally run d_load_guard (F) and schedule (cancel F; d_schedule T during a request because active_requests > 0). The branch 'calls' list still names load_model.

br:be9c978e2166 also requires the task not to be done and not to be the current task. No shown case distinguishes these; a cancel invoked from inside the running timer (re-arm path of d_idle_recent) or on an already-finished task would evaluate F while timer_pending is true.

unknowns.what: Concurrency test cannot be generated sequentially
unknowns.why: test_ensure_backend_serializes_concurrent_reloads interleaves five coroutines (four fast-path F then four locked re-checks F); the sequential scenario predicts one reload then four fast-path T. The log marks it not scored.
Assumed the 0.01s timer fires after >= 0.01s of idleness so it unloads on the first firing; event-loop early wakeup within clock resolution could instead take the re-arm branch once before unloading.

unknowns.what: Timing of the idle timer relative to request completion
unknowns.why: Timer firings are modeled as explicit _idle_unload_after calls placed after the awaited sleep; in test_active_request_blocks_idle_unload no timer exists during the request (begin cancels, none scheduled), so no firing is modeled.

unknowns.what: status test setup and get_manager singleton
unknowns.why: The status test source is truncated in the bundle; last_used_set=true and backend_loaded=true are taken from the observed state-in. get_manager (br:2f19fdb911a4) is not modeled because no test exercises it.
Errors raised by backend.load_model, initialize or backend.generate (wrapped into RuntimeError) are not modeled; in particular a failing generate still runs _end_request via hold's finally.
